text:
incident-bot: Pager: High error rate and 5xx spike for inference endpoints in us-west-2 (az1a). Signal: backend conn resets + elevated p95 latency. Alert ID: infra/az1a-inference-connreset-3070. Auto-eviction attempted.

erin-oncall: acked. I'm taking incident. pinging network and infra oncall. Can we confirm scope? % requests failing and which customers? :phone:

mike-sre: seeing ~17% 5xx at the NLB targets for az1a. Logs show a lot of `ECONNRESET` from upstream pods. Node-level dmesg shows nf_conntrack counters saturating on a subset of hosts.

tara-sre: confirmed on two node groups (g5-large-az1a and g5-small-az1a). `conntrack` table near max on those nodes. Also seeing kube-proxy CPU spikes ~90% on the same nodes.

jess-product: customers hitting inference in us-west-2 report timeouts. We have a small cohort of paying customers routed to dedicated pools in az1a — could be impacted. Sam is pulling customer telemetry.

sam-cust-eng: on it, pulling request logs. 8 customers show elevated tail latencies; two have >25% error rate. I'll open a support ticket for top two and start templated comms draft.

erin-oncall: immediate mitigations: 1) steer new traffic away from affected nodes/az if possible. 2) increase conntrack table headroom. 3) attempt graceful restart of kube-proxy on problematic nodes. Who can run the commands?

mike-sre: I can run the quick checks and bump conntrack on nodes. Commands: ```# check conntrack usage
sudo cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count
sudo cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
# bump (temporary)
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=2000000
# reload kube-proxy (daemonset restart)
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart daemonset/kube-proxy --selector=topology.kubernetes.io/zone=us-west-2a
```

tara-sre: For traffic steering: we can mark NLB targets unhealthy for the affected instances which will divert to other AZs. I'll coordinate with `infra-bot` to run target deregistration if we want immediate traffic shift. Note: this will increase load on other AZs.

erin-oncall: Do it. Prioritize customer SLOs. Tara please deregister targets for the 4 worst nodes. Add graceful drain for pods after deregister.

tara-sre: doing step 1: deregister command: ```aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:... --targets Id=i-0abcd1234 Id=i-0abcd2345``` then `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` after. I'll stage across nodes to avoid cascading.

mike-sre: bumped nf_conntrack on two nodes, values now: count=1450000 max=2000000. Kube-proxy restart in progress for zone selector. Observed kube-proxy crashloop for one node, investigating.

infra-bot: Event: target deregistration initiated by tara-sre for targets [i-0abcd1234, i-0abcd2345, i-0abcd3456, i-0abcd4567]. Expected connection drain: 300s.

erin-oncall: good. Monitoring p95 and 5xx now. Sam, update customers with ETA ~15-30m for failover and mitigation.

sam-cust-eng: Drafted comms and sent to two customers (IDs 0123, 0456). Added note about cross-AZ failover happening and asking if they can tolerate brief in-flight request failures.

mike-sre: After kube-proxy restart some nodes show kube-proxy pid cycling; digging into iptables vs ipvs mode. There's a known kernel+kube-proxy combo that causes conntrack leak on long-lived connections. We're testing switching kube-proxy to iptables mode on one canary node.

erin-oncall: If switching proxy mode fixes it, we'll roll with a narrow canary, then plan a broader patch and kernel/OS upgrade in maintenance. Is this safe for traffic?

tara-sre: Canary in az1b first to avoid touching remaining az1a capacity. But we still need to keep az1a drained until stable. Current failover reduced 5xx to ~4% across us-west-2. Good progress.

jess-product: Noting customer SLAs — ops, capture exact impacted customers and escalation level. I'll prepare internal impact note.

mike-sre: Canary switch command: ```kubectl -n kube-system edit daemonset/kube-proxy``` change `mode: "iptables"` in configmap and rollout restart for one node via nodeSelector. Monitoring for conntrack leak regression.

infra-bot: Metric alert resolved? infra/az1a-inference-connreset-3070 -> status: trigger suppressed by target deregistration and conntrack bump.

erin-oncall: We're moving to mitigation verification phase. Remaining steps: 1) confirm customer error rates decreased 2) keep targets deregistered until nodes stable 3) schedule deeper remediation (kernel/OS upgrade + kube-proxy config change) in next maintenance window.

sam-cust-eng: Customers 0123/0456 acknowledged and accepting failover. Two smaller customers require postmortem.

mike-sre: Canary looks good after iptables switch, no conntrack growth for 20m. Planning to apply iptables mode to az1a nodes in staged windows with pause between each node.

erin-oncall: handoff plan: I'm handing off incident to tara-sre for mitigation execution and patch planning. If anything regresses or new alerts fire, page `#oncall-sre`. I'll remain available.

tara-sre: ack. I'll own the rollouts and remediation. Creating follow-up ticket: INF-3070 with runbook steps, customer list, and remediation timeline.

erin-oncall: quick customer impact summary for postmortem: - Scope: us-west-2, primarily az1a nodes - Impact: up to 25% error rate for small cohort; cluster-wide p95 latency increase until failover - Root cause hypothesis: kube-proxy/ipvs conntrack leak on kernel combo with sustained long-lived connections used by inference runtime - Mitigation: NLB target deregistration (steer traffic), bump nf_conntrack, restart/reconfigure kube-proxy (iptables canary), schedule kernel/OS upgrade and full kube-proxy rollout - Next steps: postmortem + permanent kernel param and config change + test matrix for kube-proxy modes on our inference workloads

jess-product: Thanks team. I'll own the customer-facing postmortem draft and coordinate timing with comms.

erin-oncall: closing pager. Tara, please update thread when remediation scheduled. :white_check_mark:
